ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Under suitable conditions such as illumination, a certain plant cultivated in an environment with CO2 concentration of 1% is rapidly transferred to an environment with CO2 concentration of 0.003%. The changing trends of the micromolar concentrations of C3 and C5 compounds in the dark reaction of its leaves are shown in the figure. Answer the question: if this plant continues to be in the environment with CO2 concentration of 0.003%, when the concentrations of C3 and C5 compounds in the dark reaction reach stability, will the concentration of substance A be higher or lower than that of B?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the vertical axis is labeled “relative concentration,” and the horizontal axis is “time/s”; at about 200 s there is a vertical dashed line, with 1% CO2 labeled on the left side of the dashed line and 0.003% CO2 labeled on the right side. Before transfer, curve A is at a relatively high stable level, and curve B is at a relatively low stable level; after transfer to low CO2, the curve corresponding to A first decreases, and the curve corresponding to B first increases. Then reason: when CO2 concentration suddenly decreases, the reaction in which C5 fixes CO2 to form C3 weakens, so in the short term C3 decreases and C5 accumulates. From the changes in the figure, it can be judged that A corresponds to C3 compound and B corresponds to C5 compound. If it continues to be in the 0.003% CO2 environment and reaches a new stable state, the dark reaction still maintains the cycle, and the concentration of C3 compound is usually higher than that of C5 compound, so the stable concentration of A is higher than B.
